task.description: Implement lib/letflow/design/iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md (twice-reworked, PASSED) exactly: add Letflow.Admission.reserved_headroom/1 + its backing state field, add Letflow.Scheduler.sweep_task_timeout_ms/0, convert the 7 per-tenant Enum.each sweeps in lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex to bounded Task.async_stream/3, add per-task rescue at the 2 sites lacking one.

result.summary:
Implemented per the approved design, exactly as specified, with one significant BLOCKER-level finding surfaced during verification (see 'routing' below) that this design's own approval process did not catch.

1) lib/letflow/admission.ex (§3b/§7): init/1's returned state map gains a genuinely new 5th field, reserved_headroom, set from the identical reserved_headroom binding already in scope in that same init/1 clause (the same value used to compute global_cap) -- purely additive, none of the existing 4 keys' types or read/write sites changed. State-shape comment updated to 5 keys. Added reserved_headroom/1 (default server \\ __MODULE__), a GenServer.call/2 delegate mirroring try_acquire/2/release/2's exact idiom, plus a new handle_call(:reserved_headroom, _from, state) clause replying state.reserved_headroom unchanged. try_acquire/2, release/2, and every existing handle_call clause's reads/writes of global_in_use/tenants/refs/global_cap are byte-for-byte unchanged.

2) lib/letflow/scheduler.ex (§4a/§7): added sweep_task_timeout_ms/0 following the exact existing pattern of poll_interval_ms/0 (scheduler_config()[:sweep_task_timeout_ms] || @default_sweep_task_timeout_ms, default 10_000, read fresh every call, no caching).

3) lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex (§2-§7): all 7 Enum.each(schemas, ...) per-tenant loops converted to Task.async_stream/3 via a new private run_sweep/4 helper (for the 6 side-effect-only sweeps) or an inline call (for maybe_refresh_active_instances/1, which needs to reduce a sum rather than just consume side effects). Every call site sets timeout: Scheduler.sweep_task_timeout_ms(), on_timeout: :kill_task, zip_input_on_exit: true, and fully consumes the stream (Enum.each/Enum.reduce). The 6 Admission-gated sweeps use a literal @admission_gated_max_concurrency 8 (module attribute, commented as 'exactly Admission.global_cap at default config'), matching the design's explicit choice NOT to derive this one live (§3a's own arithmetic: Admission.try_acquire(:global)'s own gate is already the true ceiling regardless of this value). maybe_refresh_active_instances/1 instead calls Letflow.Admission.reserved_headroom() fresh inside its own function body every tick (never cached/hoisted) and passes that live value as max_concurrency -- per §3b's global_cap + max_concurrency = pool_size identity. Per-task rescue (§4b) added at the 2 call sites lacking an existing inline one -- the poll-and-fire loop and maybe_run_retention_sweep/2 -- via try/rescue around the with_admission/3 call, logging via a new log_task_raise/4 helper (schema:/op:/error: tagged, mirroring with_admission/3's capacity-skip log style) and returning :ok. The other 4 sweeps' existing inline try/rescue -> :ok is untouched (no redundant second rescue added, per design). A new log_task_exit/3 helper logs every {:exit, {schema_name, reason}} yield from a stream (timeout or crash) with the same schema:/op: tagging. Verified the real Task.async_stream/3 zip_input_on_exit shape against elixir/lib/task.ex source directly (not assumed from the design doc's informal prose): exit tuples are {:exit, {input, reason}}, not {input, {:exit, reason}} -- implemented to match the real API. tenant_schemas/0/fetch_tenant_schemas/0 still called exactly once per tick (AC4), schemas threaded unchanged to all 7 sweeps -- confirmed by inspection, no new call site added. Sweeps remain strictly sequential relative to each other (§2) -- only per-tenant iteration inside each sweep is now concurrent. Updated the module's own moduledoc (both the stale 'no additional rescue needed' comment, now corrected to explain why a rescue WAS added despite the pre-existing no-raise contract, and a new 'ISS-0421 addition' section documenting the two concurrency-bound classes) to keep it accurate.

EMPIRICAL POOL_SIZE CONFIRMATION: grepped config/dev.exs, config/runtime.exs, config/test.exs directly. config/dev.exs:54 sets pool_size: 10 (literal, unchanged). config/runtime.exs:113 sets pool_size: String.to_integer(System.get_env("POOL_SIZE") || "10") (default 10, unchanged). The design's §1 arithmetic (pool_size=10, reserved_headroom=2, global_cap=8) is still current -- no drift since the design was approved.

VERIFICATION (run for real, in the foreground, output read and confirmed -- not claimed):
- mix compile --warnings-as-errors: clean, no warnings, after every edit and again on the final diff.
- mix test test/letflow/admission_test.exs: 15/15 passed -- the new reserved_headroom field/accessor is fully additive and does not disturb any existing Admission behavior.
- mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs (run standalone with --seed 0 for a clean, reproducible count): 12/16 passed, 4 failed, reproducibly (same 4 tests fail on repeat runs). See BLOCKER finding below -- this is NOT a flaky-test artifact, it is a structural consequence of the approved design.
- Full mix test suite: NOT run to completion in this turn. An initial attempt exceeded the tool's foreground execution window and was explicitly stopped (TaskStop) rather than left running in the background per this project's 'no background wait for a cross-turn notification' rule -- I did not want to end this turn waiting on a background notification for a check I could not act on until the next turn regardless. The two targeted suites above (Admission + Poller, the only modules this change touches) were run to completion in the foreground and are the load-bearing evidence here. Recommend TEST-RUNNER (or REVIEWER, if it re-runs mix test itself) run the full suite as part of its own gate.

MUTATION TESTING on the reserved_headroom-drift safety property (the exact property the design's 3 rework cycles exist to protect, explicitly requested for this turn): temporarily hardcoded maybe_refresh_active_instances/1's max_concurrency to a literal 2 (poller.ex, replacing `Admission.reserved_headroom()` with `2` -- the CURRENT default reserved_headroom value, chosen deliberately so the mutation is 'silent' at today's config, exactly the drift-under-a-future-config-change hazard §3b/CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's rework-1 FAIL was about), then re-ran mix test test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs test/letflow/admission_test.exs. Result: identical failure set (the same admission-collision REQ-218 failures described below, none new, none newly-passing attributable to this specific mutation). CONFIRMED REAL COVERAGE GAP: no existing test asserts that maybe_refresh_active_instances/1's Task.async_stream max_concurrency actually tracks a non-default Admission.reserved_headroom() value (e.g. by starting an Admission instance with reserved_headroom: 5 via start_link/1 opts and asserting the sweep's observed peak concurrency is 5, not 2). The design doc itself already flags this exact class of gap in its own §3b rationale for why a live accessor beats a hardcoded-literal-plus-equality-test. Flagging this explicitly for TEST-DESIGNER (after REVIEWER) to close: a test starting a distinct, differently-configured Admission instance under its own name (mirroring admission_test.exs's own existing pattern) and asserting maybe_refresh_active_instances/1's live concurrency bound follows it. Reverted the mutation before finishing (confirmed via mix compile --warnings-as-errors and grep that the live `Admission.reserved_headroom()` call is back in place).

SELF-REVIEW: no state-transition SHAPE changed in Letflow.ProcessInstance (this change is entirely in Admission/Scheduler/Poller) -- README.md's ASCII diagram is unaffected, not touched. No migration added. mix format was not run as a separate check in this environment (no evidence mix format --check-formatted is configured differently from mix compile here) -- ran mix compile --warnings-as-errors as the available toolchain check, per the 'if not available, say so explicitly' instruction; format-check specifically was not separately invoked, noting this rather than silently claiming it.
result.routing:
Route to REVIEWER (not TEST-DESIGNER yet) with a BLOCKER-level flag, before this proceeds further. FINDING: implementing lib/letflow/design/iss0421-poller-bounded-concurrency.md exactly as approved breaks 4 existing, previously-passing REQ-218 acceptance tests in test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs: 'REQ-218 AC1' (forced-zero admission cap), 'REQ-218 AC2' (cap of exactly 1 still drains all schemas sequentially), 'REQ-218 AC3 (per-schema clause)' (a rejected schema's other ops still proceed), and 'REQ-218 AC5' (existing per-operation rescue still catches its own raise with no leak) -- all reproducibly, not flakily (re-run with --seed 0, same 4 fail every time). ROOT CAUSE: REQ-218's own test suite encodes, in its own code comments (poller_test.exs's AC2 describe block: 'A single, sequential caller (Poller) never holds more than one admission unit at a time... so with global_cap == 1 and NO concurrent contender, Poller's own acquire/release round trips never collide with each other -- every attempt succeeds'), an invariant that ISS-0421's approved design deliberately and structurally breaks: Poller can now hold up to @admission_gated_max_concurrency (8) admission units concurrently within one sweep, by design. All 4 failing tests deliberately configure a very low effective global_cap (pool_size: 3, reserved_headroom: 2 -> global_cap: 1) specifically to exercise REQ-218's fairness/no-self-collision guarantees -- exactly the scenario where max_concurrency (8) now exceeds the live global_cap (1), so multiple of Poller's OWN concurrently-dispatched tasks for the SAME sweep race each other for the sole slot, and whichever lose get skipped-and-logged with NO retry (Task.async_stream does not retry a rejected/skipped item -- it only starts the NEXT schema in the list as a slot frees). Under the old Enum.each, Poller only ever held at most 1 admission unit at a time by construction, so this self-collision was structurally impossible; only an external HTTP contender could ever cause a rejection, and REQ-218's tests distinguish 'external contention -> some skips, acceptable' (AC3, which still passes) from 'no external contention -> everything eventually succeeds' (AC1/AC2, which now fail because Poller became its own contender). CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's 3 review cycles were correctly, narrowly focused on the reserved_headroom state-field/accessor correctness gap (per its own gate_history) and did not check this design's interaction with REQ-218's already-decided, already-tested guarantees -- this is a genuine gap in the design review, not an ELIXIR-DEV implementation deviation (I implemented §3a's literal max_concurrency: 8 exactly as specified; the design itself, correctly implemented, is what produces this regression). This is exactly a 'decision-record consistency' question per REVIEWER's own gate scope (REQ-218 is a done, previously-signed-off requirement whose test suite this change now contradicts) -- I have not modified, and should not unilaterally modify, test/letflow/scheduler/poller_test.exs myself to make these pass, since that would be silently re-deciding what REQ-218 already settled rather than getting sign-off first. REVIEWER has two live options as I see it, neither of which is mine to pick: (a) send this back to CODE-DESIGNER for a rework that bounds max_concurrency for the 6 Admission-gated sweeps by min(8, some live Admission accessor) rather than a hardcoded 8, restoring 'Poller never exceeds live global_cap concurrently' as an invariant (this would need a new Admission.global_cap/1 accessor, mirroring reserved_headroom/1's now-established pattern) -- at the cost of one more rework cycle and a 4th CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR pass; or (b) accept this as an intentional, understood behavior change (Poller's own admission attempts within a sweep can now self-collide when max_concurrency > live global_cap, which is fine at the real deployed default of 8 with typical tenant counts, and REQ-218's 4 affected tests get explicitly revised by TEST-DESIGNER to assert the NEW guarantee -- e.g. 'eventually converges given enough ticks' or 'no self-collision only when global_cap >= max_concurrency' -- rather than the old, now-superseded 'every attempt always succeeds regardless of cap' claim. Either way, this needs REVIEWER's explicit sign-off before TEST-DESIGNER touches poller_test.exs, per core-directives' 'every producing step has a validating step' and CLAUDE.md's 'don't silently re-decide what a decision record already settled.'

SECURITY-REVIEWER ROUTING DECISION: not required as a hard gate before REVIEWER for this change, checked directly against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md's actual criteria rather than assumed either way. INV-1 (tenant data isolation) does not apply: no new/changed Ecto schema, no migration, no query gains or loses :prefix scoping -- the only DB-adjacent code touched (Task.async_stream wrapping) does not change which schema any existing query targets, only how many of the existing per-schema calls run concurrently. INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 are stage-gated (S4/S5, not yet applicable) and this change touches no API response shaping or sandboxed scripting. INV-4 (secrets by reference) does not apply -- no secret material is read, logged, or threaded anywhere in this diff; the new Logger.warning/2 calls log only schema_name (already logged today by with_admission/3's existing capacity-skip warning) and op/error/reason atoms/strings, never a secret. INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) does not apply -- zero Repo.query/Ecto.Adapters.SQL.query calls added or changed. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) is the one invariant genuinely relevant here, and this change strictly IMPROVES its posture rather than weakening it: it adds 2 new rescue sites (poll-and-fire, retention) precisely because Task.async_stream's larger failure blast radius made the pre-existing no-raise contracts a bigger bet, and every stream is fully consumed with on_timeout: :kill_task so no timeout can crash the Poller GenServer itself. Net: this is a scheduler/admission-control internals change, not a tenant-data-path change (no migration, no API route, no response shaping, no secret handling) -- REVIEWER alone is the correct next gate, consistent with security-reviewer.md's own scope test.

gate_history.notes: reserved_headroom is now specified as a genuinely new, fifth Letflow.Admission state field, captured in init/1 from the same binding used to compute global_cap; the reserved_headroom/1 accessor's handle_call clause reads this newly-populated field, not a phantom one. Per-instance algebraic identity explicitly covers a start_link/1 opts-overridden test instance. Design is buildable as specified; routed to ELIXIR-DEV.
